messages:
maya: Noticed a weird pattern on us-east yesterday: websocket sessions marked as "active" in the console but client-side shows immediate RST and reconnect. Billing doubled for a short window. Anyone seen WS RST from nginx/ILB combo?

leo: Which stack? nginx as edge then envoy? Did you get tcpdump?

maya: nginx edge -> gce ILB -> envoy -> runtime. I grabbed a tcpdump: RST from nginx at ~35s idle, client reconnects 200ms later. Runtime logs never emit a connection close so console keeps the session live until higher-level timeout.

ashwin: Runtime only promotes CLOSED on application-level EOF. We treat early RST as noisy network unless socket library surfaces it. That explains console discrepancy.

ui: This is confusing for users. Console shows green dot and streaming graphs while client library shows reconnect loop. We should show a transient state like "idle-probed (rst)" and surface last-packet metadata.

maya: Example tcpdump lines: 
```
08:22:11.001 IP 10.1.2.3.443 > 10.2.3.4.52344: RST, seq 0
08:22:11.003 IP 10.2.3.4.52344 > 10.1.2.3.443: SYN
```
Runtime logs around that time: 
```
[2026-03-19T08:22:11.010Z] ws: conn=xyz active=true last_send=2026-03-19T08:21:38Z
# no close event for ~6s
[2026-03-19T08:22:17.200Z] ws: client reconnect conn=xyz-1 resume=true
```

leo: Risk: if we mark session closed on RST, resume might create a new session and break sticky routing semantics. But leaving it visible-as-active breaks telemetry and billing.

ashwin: Proposal: (1) emit a new metric ws_idle_rst tagged with layer=(nginx|ilb|envoy), route, tenant; (2) console-only state change to "idle-probed (rst)" behind a FF; (3) add a short grace TTL for resume tokens when we detect RST so resume still works for normal reconnects.

ui: For UX, console should also show a small hint: "Upstream RST observed; this session may have been terminated by a proxy. Tokens during this window are under investigation."

billing-bot: Created billing task BL-562 to investigate duplicate windows and to add idempotency guard for short RST windows (maya assigned)

maya: I sketched a runtime change: detect socket error EINTR/EPIPE/RST and call mark_console_stale(session) w/ reason="tcp_rst". Keep resume_token valid for 10s. Snippet: 
```
if (socket_error == RST || socket_error == EPIPE) {
  emit("ws_idle_rst", {layer, route, tenant});
  mark_console_state(session, "idle_probed_rst");
  extend_resume_ttl(session, 10s);
}
```

leo: Add histogram metric for time-to-surface (tcp-event -> console-state). We want to measure how often runtime misses the event.

sre-bot: Alert created: AL-991 if ws_idle_rst_rate > 0.3% of active sessions over 5m

ashwin: Rollout plan: console-only FF first in us-west-canary for 48h, collect metrics and UX feedback, then enable in prod. Do NOT change routing logic until RFC.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated: runtime/patch-2098 -> us-west-canary at 2026-03-21T02:00:00Z

maya: Canary report after 6h: ws_idle_rst events concentrated on edge-nginx instances behind ILB, ~0.12% of sessions, dashboard tile added to staging. No resume breakages observed with 10s TTL.

leo: Good. Next: coordinate with infra docs to recommend tcp_keepalive tuning on nginx and ILB TTL config. Also, update routing docs about "probe-terminated" vs "app-terminated" session semantics.

ashwin: I'll draft RFC to decide final routing semantics (immediate failover vs sticky-resume-with-grace). RFC will include telemetry requirements and impact on quota counting.

ui: Can we add a small UI control to toggle whether to include "probe-terminated" windows in cost graphs? That will help customers while we debug infra.

billing-bot: BL-562 updated: status=assigned, runtime-pr=2098 referenced

maya: Thanks team. Keeping FF on for 72h, will post follow-up with aggregate histograms and pcap samples.

leo: tag me if you need sample pcaps or help with nginx conf.

maya: will do. closing loop once RFC is up.
